parameters.name: StationId
parameters.description:
StationId is a unique identifier for a station. A format example is "6.10.0". You can also
give multiple stations separated with comma. Example: "6.10.0,12.209.0"

parameters.name: Parameter
parameters.description:
Parameter can be a valid parameterId (number) or parameter name as a text. Example "1003" or "vanntemperatur". You can also
give multiple parameters separated with comma. Example: "1000,1001"

parameters.name: ResolutionTime
parameters.description:
Resolution time can be entered as text or a number in minutes, valid resolutions are "day" and "hour" (or "1440" and "60"). 
For raw/instantaneous data as it is measured, use "inst" (or "0").

parameters.name: VersionNumber
parameters.description:
The api also supports series with more than one version. If a series has more version can be found in metadata search.
If the VersionNumber is not specified, and it only exists one version, this version of the series is returned.
If a series has more than one version, the version to be returned can be specified here, else
the system returns the version with the newest data.

parameters.name: ReferenceTime
parameters.description: Reference time is the time range to get observations. If left empty, only the last known observation is returned. A reference time is build up by using datetime(s) and period(s). Period = P and DateTime = T Datetime(T) - A datetime given in ISO-8601. Example “2019-01-12T19:00” Period(P) - A period given in ISO-8601. Example “P3D” (period of 3 days) Possible combinations: T/T - Will give all observations between the two datetimes. T/ - Will give all observations from this datetime and to the latest value. /T - Will give all observations prior to this datetime. You can also use period and datetime together.Period is then relative to the datetime. P/T - example “P2D/2019-04-05” T/P - example “2019-04-05T09:00/PT12H” You can also use period alone or together with another period. Period(s) are then relative to now. P/ - example “P2D/” /P - example “/P24D” P/P - example “-P4D/P5D” (also allows negative periods only if two periods are combined) For more information, see user documentation.

parameters.name: QualityTypes
parameters.description:
The Quality Types is indicating if the observation is controlled. Enter values separated with comma like 2,3 
If not entered all observations are returned
Unknown=0,
Uncontrolled=1,
PrimaryControlled=2,
SecondaryControlled=3

parameters.name: Method
parameters.description:
Method for aggregation for the time series
Added for future usage where more method types can be supported for a time series.
Currently the method is set by the default method given by the combination of resolutiontime and parameter.
Resolutiontime instantaneous (0) always gives method "Instantaneous"
Resolutiontime hour and day gives aggregation type "Mean" for all parameters, except precipitation that gives aggregation method "Sum".

parameters.name: TimeOffset
parameters.description:
TimeOffset is added for future usage where maybe time series with the resolution time day, can be offered with a time offset.
Currently the only time offset supported is 0 (PT0H), and this value the will be chosen by default.
When the time offset is 0, it means that a day is defined to start 0 am. The day is always refered to with the timestamp 11am (UTC-0)

parameters.name: CorrectionTypes
parameters.description:
The Correction Types is indicating if a observation is changed/corrected. Enter values separated with comma like 1,4,5 
 If not entered, all observations are returned
 0: No changes
 1: Manual- or ice correction
 2: Interpolation
 3: Value computed with models or/and other series
 4: Daily mean computed with arithmetic mean. (Only used on series where we normally should use discharge curve)
 5: Smooth negative value. (Only used with inflow)
 6: Dry pipe. (Only used with groundwater data)
 7: Ice in pipe. (Only used with groundwater data)
 8: Damaged pipe. (Only used with groundwater data)
 9: Pumping. (Only used with groundwater data)
 11: Start/end value linear adjustment
 12: Incomplete data source
 13: The value is calculated based on a similar station or a station close by. The value is adjusted according to the statistical differences between the original station and the replacement station
 14: The value is missing, and is only calculated based on statistical information for the data series.
 15: The value is the result of a calculation that ended in Nan(not a number) or +/-Inf. (Technically, the value needs to be outside the interval -1e+300 to +1e0399.)
 16: Value fetched from rejected period.
